bug_semantics: TemplateContext.GetMemberAccessor cached one accessor per runtime Type, while TypedObjectAccessor captured the context's then-current MemberFilter and eagerly precomputed the exposed field/property set. After a permissive render populated that cache, resetting and reusing the same TemplateContext under a tighter MemberFilter returned the stale permissive accessor. ScriptMemberExpression therefore continued to read, and potentially write, members that the later sandbox policy denied, enabling cross-request or cross-tenant policy bypass when contexts were reused.
flaw_origin: Commit ace7a0ebafa6d01500f83c35975cde38d559fa3d added TemplateContext.MemberFilter and threaded it into the precomputed TypedObjectAccessor without changing the existing Dictionary<Type, IObjectAccessor> cache key or invalidation behavior. That commit is the first one in which a Type-only cached accessor can embody a context-specific filter policy.
ai_marker: absent on BIC ace7a0ebafa6d01500f83c35975cde38d559fa3d: git cat-file -p shows human author and committer Alexandre Mutel <alexandre_mutel@live.com> and the single-line subject only, with no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/scriban/scriban/security/advisories/GHSA-5wr9-m6jw-xx44 documents the Type-only _memberAccessors cache, filter-bearing TypedObjectAccessor, Reset omission, stale-accessor PoC, affected versions <=6.6.0, and patched version 7.0.0. In the validated clone, `git show --format=fuller --patch ace7a0ebafa6d01500f83c35975cde38d559fa3d -- src/Scriban/TemplateContext.cs src/Scriban/Runtime/Accessors/TypedObjectAccessor.cs` shows the BIC adding MemberFilter, storing it in TypedObjectAccessor, applying it while PrepareMembers builds _members, and changing construction to `new TypedObjectAccessor(type, MemberFilter, MemberRenamer)` while GetMemberAccessor still caches solely by Type. `git log --all --reverse -S'public MemberFilterDelegate MemberFilter' -- src/Scriban/TemplateContext.cs` and `git log -L 691,691:src/Scriban/TemplateContext.cs ace7a0e...` identify ace7a0e as the first writer of that vulnerable coupling. Direct parent check `git grep -n -E 'MemberFilter|_memberAccessors|new TypedObjectAccessor' c525ebfc8bfb31853da2e0280d2a24045893badb -- src/Scriban/TemplateContext.cs src/Scriban/Runtime/Accessors/TypedObjectAccessor.cs` finds the Type-only cache and `new TypedObjectAccessor(type, MemberRenamer)` but no MemberFilter at all, proving this advisory flaw absent in the immediate parent. `git show ace7a0e...:src/Scriban/Template.cs` lines 159-168 also shows Render(TemplateContext) was already reusable and cleared its output, so the 2021 addition of Reset is not the first causal commit. `git show --format=fuller --patch 8180fb6cd1f6c2727c99f8f5a745a0b991b06cfc` shows the direct fix adding `_memberAccessors.Clear()` to Reset plus a regression test that renders permissively, resets, tightens MemberFilter, and verifies property_b is rejected. Release checks: `git for-each-ref --no-contains=ace7a0e... --sort=-creatordate refs/tags` identifies v0.15.0 as the last pre-BIC tag; tags containing the BIC begin at v0.16.0. `git rev-parse '6.6.0^{commit}' '7.0.0^{commit}'` resolves b5ac4bf30459fdc76964e3f751e16f7e96079ea7 and 25d148a104dd4d679a1a1932442616599e003c2f; `git merge-base --is-ancestor 8180fb6... 7.0.0` exits 0 while the same command for 6.6.0 exits 1, and `git tag --contains 8180fb6... --sort=version:refname` starts at 7.0.0. Finally, `git cat-file -p ace7a0e...` gives one parent c525ebf..., human author/committer Alexandre Mutel, and no AI marker in the BIC commit object.
reasoning: The vulnerability requires the conjunction of an existing Type-only accessor cache and a filter-dependent, precomputed accessor. The cache predates the flaw, but ace7a0e is the smallest commit that creates that conjunction: its parent cannot exhibit a MemberFilter bypass because TemplateContext has no MemberFilter, while ace7a0e adds both the policy and its capture into cached accessors. The later Reset commit made pooled reuse explicit but was not required to reuse Render(TemplateContext), so treating Reset as the introducer would be too late. The single-parent BIC is not a squash, move, refactor, revert, release, or backport. The direct security fix is 8180fb6, released first in 7.0.0, and the BIC commit object contains no AI evidence; therefore the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
